props.gloss_en: Shmuel: they taught [that the thigh is forbidden] only where [the nerve] was cooked in it
but [if] it was roasted in it -- one peels and eats until he reaches the nerve
Rav Huna: a kid roasted with its fat -- it is forbidden to eat even from the tip of its ear
fat is different, for it permeates
an incident before R' Yochanan in the synagogue of Maon, a kid roasted with its fat; he said: one peels and eats until he reaches its fat
that one [the kid] was lean
Rav Huna bar Yehuda: it was a kidney with its fat, and he permitted it
Ravin bar Rav Adda: it was a kilkhit in a stewpot; R' Yochanan said to them: let an Aramean cook taste it
the baraita: a pot in which one cooked meat -- he should not cook milk in it, and if he cooked -- by imparting flavor
teruma -- he should not cook non-sacred food in it, and if he cooked -- by imparting flavor
Rava: now that R' Yochanan said we rely on an Aramean cook, here too [meat in milk] we rely on an Aramean cook
Rava: the Sages spoke of taste, the Sages spoke of the gentile cook, and the Sages spoke of sixty
hence, kind with not its kind, of the permitted -- by taste
of the forbidden -- by the gentile cook
and kind with its kind, where one cannot ascertain the taste -- by sixty
or else kind with not its kind, of the forbidden, where there is no gentile cook -- by sixty
those thighs that were salted at the Exilarch's with the sciatic nerve -- Ravina forbade
Rav Acha bar Rav Ashi permitted; [Mar bar Rav Ashi:] my father permits
Shmuel: a salted item is like a boiling one
a pickled item is like a cooked one
and if you say: what is the 'like boiling' that he said? like boiling of cooking
since he said 'pickled is like cooked', it follows that he spoke of boiling of roasting
R' Chanina: when they assess, they assess with the broth, the sediment, the pieces and the pot
some say: [with] the pot itself
and some say: [with] what the pot absorbed
R' Yochanan: all the prohibitions in the Torah -- they are assessed as if they were onion and leek
Abaye: the Sages assessed that nothing among prohibitions imparts flavor more than onion and leek
Rav Nachman: the nerve -- in sixty
and the nerve is not of the count
the udder -- in sixty
and the udder is of the count
the egg -- in sixty
and the egg is not of the count
R' Yitzchak b. R' Mesharshiya: and the udder itself is forbidden
and if it fell into another pot -- it forbids
when we assess, we assess by [the udder] itself
or we assess by what came out of it
the Sages made it [the udder] like a piece of a carcass
